overview: This entry is really two physical parts sold and used together: a small hobby-sized solar panel, and a separate charge-controller board that sits between the panel and a rechargeable battery. The panel alone is just an unregulated power source — its open-circuit voltage in bright sun can exceed what a Li-ion/LiPo cell can safely accept, and at night it becomes a path for the battery to drain backward through it. The controller board fixes both problems: it tapers charge current as the battery approaches full (the same constant-current/constant-voltage idea as a TP4056 module, just fed by a variable solar source instead of a steady USB 5V), and it blocks reverse current flow with a diode or MOSFET when the panel isn't producing. Most hobby-tier boards use simple PWM or linear regulation rather than true MPPT, so don't expect lab-grade efficiency in partial sun.
simpleSummary: A small solar panel paired with a controller board that safely turns its variable sunlight-powered output into a proper battery charge.

specifications.panelType: Small hobby polycrystalline or monocrystalline panel
specifications.openCircuitVoltage: ~5-6V Voc for a 'nominal 5V/6V' panel — well above battery voltage when unloaded in bright sun
specifications.controllerFunction: Regulates panel output, blocks reverse night-time drain, and tapers charge current as the battery nears full
specifications.regulationMethod: PWM or simple linear regulation on most hobby boards (rarely true MPPT)
specifications.regulatedOutputVoltage: Tracks the battery chemistry's safe charge voltage (e.g. 4.2V max for single-cell Li-ion/LiPo)
specifications.maxChargeCurrent: Panel-dependent, commonly a few hundred mA on small hobby setups
specifications.reverseProtection: Blocking diode or MOSFET prevents the battery discharging back through the panel at night

pinMap.name: PANEL+
pinMap.function: Positive output from the solar panel, feeding into the charge controller's input.
pinMap.voltageRange: 0-6V depending on light level (varies continuously through the day)
pinMap.currentLimit: Panel-dependent, typically well under 1A on hobby panels
pinMap.gotcha: An unloaded small panel in direct sun can output more than its rated voltage — never wire it straight to a bare LiPo cell without the controller in between.

pinMap.name: PANEL-
pinMap.function: Negative/return connection from the solar panel to the controller.

pinMap.name: BAT+
pinMap.function: Battery positive terminal — connects to the cell or pack being charged.
pinMap.currentLimit: Charge current, typically a few hundred mA
pinMap.gotcha: Many budget controller boards have no low-voltage cutoff on this side — pairing one with an unprotected cell risks over-discharge on cloudy days when charge current can't keep up with a connected load.

pinMap.name: LOAD+
pinMap.function: Output terminal for powering a device directly off the regulated battery/controller rail.
pinMap.gotcha: LOAD+ is usually just tied to BAT+ on budget boards — it isn't a separately stabilized rail, so it sags right along with the battery as it discharges.

pinMap.name: LOAD-
pinMap.function: Ground return for the load output.

useCases.title: Solar-powered garden/soil sensor node
useCases.scenario: Trickle-charge a small LiPo through the day so a low-power sensor node can log soil moisture indefinitely without a wired power supply.

useCases.title: Off-grid weather station
useCases.scenario: Power a microcontroller and sensor suite directly from LOAD+/LOAD- while the panel keeps the buffer battery topped up.

useCases.title: Window-sill trickle charger
useCases.scenario: Keep a standby robot or backup battery pack topped off using ambient daylight through a window, as a slower alternative to a USB charger.

useCases.title: Solar-assisted mailbox/driveway notifier
useCases.scenario: Run a remote low-power sensor and radio module entirely off solar + battery where running mains power isn't practical.

useCases.title: Idle-time solar top-up for a small rover
useCases.scenario: Mount a panel on a robot's chassis so it recovers some charge whenever it's parked in the sun between missions.
useCases.difficulty: Advanced (panel placement and weight tradeoffs on a moving platform)

commonlyPairedWith: tp4056 (USB charging alternative for cloudy days or indoor charging)
oftenConfusedWith: tp4056 (USB-input charging module vs this solar-input charging module — different input source, similar overcharge-protection role)
a bare solar panel with no controller at all (offers no overcharge or reverse-drain protection)
oftenUpgradedTo: MPPT solar charge controllers for meaningfully better efficiency in partial or changing sunlight

beginnerMistakes: Wiring a raw panel directly to a LiPo cell with no controller in between, risking overvoltage in bright, low-load conditions.
Expecting linear output as clouds pass or the panel is partially shaded — output can drop far more than the shaded fraction would suggest.
Sizing a panel too small for the load, so the battery net-drains over a multi-day overcast stretch even though it 'charges' on sunny days.
Mounting the panel in a fixed spot that gets shaded part of the day instead of accounting for the sun's path.
Ignoring the controller board's own quiescent current draw, which matters on very small, very low-power systems.
